As the phone app, Tetra shows its own call screen and buzzes when they answer. The phone\'s own call recording is not shown then.

Calls recorded on the computer show here. A phone app cannot record a call\'s other side on Android; when the call\'s sound is on the computer, its call bubble can.
Give people a heart in Contacts and they show here: one tap calls, holding opens them.
Hold a key on the keypad to call: 1 is voicemail.
Calls from these are declined before they ring, on this phone; the same list is on the tablet and the computer. A * at the end takes a whole range (69800*).
It reaches farther and through more walls; 5 GHz is much faster in the same room or the next. In the phone\'s hotspot settings, 5 GHz can be chosen if every device has it.
It reaches farther and through more walls; 5 GHz is much faster in the same room or the next. Most routers offer both: use 5 GHz where it reaches.
Walls, floors and large furniture between you and the phone weaken it, concrete and metal most. Keep the phone high and uncovered — not in a pocket, a bag or under a pillow — and nearer.

Walls, floors and large furniture between you and the router weaken it, concrete and metal most. Raise the router, move it toward the middle of the home, out of cabinets and away from the TV, mirrors, metal, aquariums and the microwave.
Enough for the web; video calls may stutter. A room nearer, or the phone higher, helps.

resources.string: %1$s of %2$s used, %3$d days before the renewal. What comes now may be slower or cost extra, as the carrier\'s terms say.
At your usual pace the %1$s run out before %2$s. To last, stay near %3$s a day.
At your usual pace you will use about %1$s of %2$s: %3$s to spare. You could use up to %4$s a day and still make it.

Most of the plan goes to the tablet and the computer. Their updates, downloads, backups and video fill it fastest: leave those for a Wi-Fi that is not the phone\'s, or set them to pause on metered networks (Android and most computers can).
A weekend day %1$s, a workday %2$s (×%3$s): with no Wi-Fi at work to lean on, weekends are where a Wi-Fi saves the most.
A workday %1$s, a weekend day %2$s: the commute and work hours are where the plan goes.
Mostly app updates. In the Play Store › Settings › Network preferences, app updates can be set to Wi-Fi only.
%1$s of it in the background. Android\'s settings for the app can stop its background data (tap it in Apps).
The app using the most of the plan, mostly while open. Its own settings may have a data saver or a lower video quality.
Over twice your average of %1$s. Tap that day\'s bar to see which apps it was.
Live speed in the status bar
Turn on Usage access so Data can count each app\'s data. It stays on your devices.
The phone\'s plan arrives with Local Sync once Data is set up on the phone.
Tell Data your plan: its size and when it renews, for warnings and a daily budget.
Apps · %1$s (tap the bar again for all)

The ring: how much of the limit the cycle has used (counting from what you typed from the carrier, if you did). Budget: what is left shared over the days left, today included — staying under it, the plan lasts. Forecast: where your usual days take you by the renewal.

Each bar is a day (an hour in Day, a month in Year), stacked: mobile data (lime), the hotspot (orange) — on the phone what it shared, on the tablet and the computer what they used through it — and Wi-Fi (blue). Tap a bar for its apps; tap it again for all. Faint bars: the days to come, each the median of the same weekday over the last three weeks. Dashed line: your average day, everything shown counted. Red dots: signal drops. ‹ › go back and forth in time.
faint: the days to come, from your usual weekdays
The tablet\'s and the computer\'s counts have not come yet (Local Sync).
Not counted by them: %1$s (a guest, hours they were off, overheads)

The solid line adds up the plan\'s data day by day since %1$s; the dashed one carries it on with your usual days to the renewal; the top line is the limit. If the dashed line crosses it, the limit comes before the renewal — the day\'s budget above says how much a day would last.

The phone\'s mobile data, as the plan counts it. Average: the days so far, today left out. Workdays and weekends: the typical (median) day of each over the last three weeks, so one odd day does not pull it. Through the hotspot: the share of the mobile data the phone gave to other devices. On Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi\'s share of everything this device used.

This device\'s data. Average: the days so far, today left out. Workdays and weekends: the typical (median) day of each over the last three weeks, so one odd day does not pull it. Over the phone\'s hotspot: the share of this device\'s Wi-Fi that was the phone\'s hotspot. On Wi-Fi: Wi-Fi\'s share of everything this device used.
Worked out from your own days: the pace, where the data goes, the weekdays and the apps. Only information — Data changes nothing; each line says where you could change it yourself.
In front %1$s · in the background %2$s · roaming %3$s
Android\'s settings for this app (background data)
Nothing counted yet. The tablet\'s and the computer\'s counts arrive with Local Sync.

The phone counts all its hotspot carried; the tablet and the computer each count what they used over it. The difference: another device on the hotspot, hours they were off or not counting, and the network\'s own overheads. Tetra\'s own sync between your devices never reaches the mobile network and is not counted.
Data used between Start and Stop: a trip, a film. A restart while counting loses the count.
Data counts how much mobile data and Wi-Fi each app uses, warns you before your plan runs out, and shows the phone, the tablet and the computer together.
To count each app, it reads Android\'s own usage statistics. Everything stays on your devices: Tetra sends it only to your own tablet and computer, with Local Sync, and to no one else.

Android asks you to switch this on yourself, in its settings: on Tetra\'s page there, turn on \"Permit usage access\" (it may say \"Permit access to app usage data\"; on Xiaomi the list is \"Apps with usage access\").
Skip it and Data shows only today\'s totals.
\"Unlimited\" plans have a fair-use limit in their terms (often a few hundred GB). The number is in your carrier\'s terms.
No warnings; the graphs and the per-app lists stay.
Carry what is left to the next cycle (rollover)
A fixed daily quota (optional; empty = what is left over the days left)
In the EU, roaming counts against my plan (as at home)
Outside the EU: a day pass?

Abroad, Data tells you when roaming begins, the day\'s first MB (when a day pass starts costing), at 80 % and 100 % of the pass, and when you are back — each with a button to Android\'s switch to turn data roaming off. Android lets no app switch it off by itself.
Your carrier\'s app or SMS says how much you have used this cycle. Type it to start level with it (optional): Data then counts from there.
Write a size, as 41 GB or 800 MB
When a day\'s budget is passed
The download and upload speed as the status bar\'s icon, while the screen is on (it stops in your pocket, so it costs next to nothing).

To list the Wi-Fi networks around and rate their channels, Android needs the location permission and Location switched on — only while Data\'s Signal page is open. Optional: the signal meter itself needs nothing.
Ready. No limit; Data counts and shows.
Change any of it later from Data\'s ⋯ › Setup, or Settings › Data.
Write a size, as 300 GB or 800 MB
No radio: the cable is as good as it gets
Sound: beeps faster as the signal grows

How the paired computer is connected now, read from it every few seconds. The test sends 20 MB each way between this device and the computer over your network (no internet) and pings it 20 times: the speed of the Wi-Fi, the hotspot or the cable between you, and how many packets were lost. Each test keeps how both ends were connected, so Ethernet, Wi-Fi and the hotspot can be compared.
Not answering (is Tetra open on it, on the same network?)
To hear the networks around, Android needs the location permission (only while this page is open).

Each curve is a network heard around, as wide as the channels it uses and as tall as it is strong; yours is lime, with ✓. The metres are a rough guess from the signal alone (walls make networks look farther). Networks that overlap share the air and slow each other down. Android lets an app listen 4 times in 2 minutes.

Stand somewhere and save it: ten seconds of the signal, averaged, and the speed to the computer. Then move the router (or the phone that is the hotspot), give the round a new name, and save the same spots again: the rounds side by side say which place was best.

Lost or very weak signal, from Android\'s own callbacks on the phone and the tablet and from the computer: mobile data lost, no service, a fall to 3G, Wi-Fi lost and back within ten minutes, the computer off the hotspot. Recorded while Tetra runs; hours it was not running are gaps, not \"no drops\". Today\'s arrive with the next hourly look.

All of your %1$s is used, %2$d days before the plan renews.

%1$s used of your %2$s · %3$s left for %4$d days.
In the EU: as at home, but your plan does not count it.
In the EU: as at home, counted against your plan.
Your day pass: %1$s for %2$s a day.
Back home. Data roaming is still ON — turn it off for the next trip?
The first roaming data today — today counts as a day of your pass (%1$s for %2$s).
%1$s of today\'s %2$s. More may cost extra or be slow.
